myths.Agent_1:
Long ago, before the towering mountains had voices, they stood in absolute silence. They were the silent guardians of the earth, strictly forbidden by the sky gods to speak, lest their deep rumblings shatter the fragile sky. 

Among the peaks lived Aethel, a wind-spirit who loved a mortal shepherd named Kael. Kael would play his wooden flute every evening, and Aethel would dance to the melodies, unseen but felt in the gentle breeze. 

One harsh, unforgiving winter, Kael perished in a sudden blizzard. Heartbroken, Aethel wept, but the wind has no voice to mourn. Desperate to keep Kael’s memory alive, she stole the last breath from his frozen lips, containing the final note of his flute. 

She carried the note to the oldest mountain, pleading with the stone to hold it forever. Touched by her deep grief, the mountain defied the sky gods. It swallowed the note, letting it bounce against its hollow caverns. 

When Aethel cried out her sorrow, the mountain called back, mimicking her grief to comfort her. Soon, all the other mountains learned this trick. Thus, the magnificent echo was born—a permanent monument of stone and air, ensuring that no cry into the void goes unanswered.
myths.Agent_2:
Long ago, before the mountains had voices, lived a spirit named Aella. She was the weaver of wind, responsible for guiding the breeze through the valleys. Aella loved a mortal shepherd named Kael, who played the most beautiful melodies on his reed flute. Every evening, Aella would carry his music across the lands, ensuring every creature could hear it.

One day, the God of Silence, enraged by the constant noise, stole Kael’s flute and turned the shepherd into stone at the peak of the highest mountain. Heartbroken, Aella wept. She begged the God of Silence to restore him, but he refused, declaring that the mountains would remain quiet forever.

Defiant, Aella used all her magic to weave her own essence into the stone. She could not bring Kael back to life, but she could give the rocks a memory. Now, whenever someone shouts into a canyon or plays a melody near the cliffs, Aella’s spirit catches the sound and throws it back. She is now forever searching for Kael’s lost song. And thus, the phenomenon of the echo was finally born into the world, a tragic, eternal reminder of a wind spirit’s pure devotion to a simple shepherd’s silenced melody.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before the world had echoes, the towering mountains were silent sentinels, strictly forbidden to speak by the jealous Sky Gods. Among these quiet peaks danced Aella, a wind spirit deeply in love with a mortal shepherd named Kael. Every evening, Kael played his wooden flute, and Aella would carry his beautiful melodies across the alpine meadows, defying the heavy silence. 

Tragedy struck when a sudden, unforgiving blizzard claimed Kael’s life. The Sky Gods rejoiced, believing the eternal quiet was finally restored. But Aella, heartbroken and defiant, refused to let Kael’s memory fade into the void. She caught the final, frozen breath from his lips—the last note of his flute—and carried it to the oldest, most ancient mountain. 

Weeping, she begged the stone to harbor the sound. Moved by her profound grief, the mountain chose to defy the Sky Gods. It swallowed the note deep into its hollow caverns. To protect the melody, Aella bound her own immortal essence into the rock. Now, whenever a wanderer cries out or plays a tune near the cliffs, Aella’s spirit awakens within the stone. She calls back, mimicking the sound, forever searching for Kael’s lost song. Thus, the echo was born—a monument of wind and stone, ensuring no voice is ever truly alone.
myths.Agent_1: Myth: Long ago, before the canyons had voices, the God of Silence ruled the jagged mountain peaks, demanding absolute, unbroken quiet. Aella, a mischievous wind-weaver, defied this decree by falling in love with a mortal stone-carver named Kael. Kael did not play a wooden flute; instead, he chipped away at the barren rocks, his hammer and chisel ringing out in rhythmic, joyful melodies that delighted the wind. Enraged by this constant noise, the God of Silence struck Kael down, transforming him into a hollow, lifeless pillar of stone at the edge of the deepest gorge. Devastated, Aella refused to let Kael's music fade into the void. She could not undo the divine curse, so she made the ultimate sacrifice. She surrendered her physical form, weaving her ethereal essence directly into the rushing air currents of the gorge. She swept through the hollow pillar that was once her beloved, transforming his stony shell into a monumental instrument. Whenever she blew through the weathered cracks, a hauntingly beautiful melody echoed across the world, shattering the God’s absolute rule. To this day, the wind whistling through canyon walls is Aella breathing life into Kael, their defiant love singing eternally.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the deep canyons scarred the earth, Aella, the tempest-weaver, fell in love with Kael, a master stone-carver. Kael wished to bridge the gap between their realms, so he began carving a magnificent staircase of white marble reaching toward the heavens, hoping to meet Aella in the sky. The Sky Gods, enraged by a mortal’s hubris, shattered the staircase with a deafening thunderbolt. The colossal structure collapsed inward, violently tearing open the earth and forming a dark, endless labyrinth of canyons. Kael was swallowed by the depths, trapped beneath millions of tons of jagged rock. 

Desperate and heartbroken, Aella abandoned the open skies. She plunged into the dark fissures, transforming her gentle breezes into fierce, howling gales. For centuries, she has swept through the narrow gorges, relentlessly eroding the stone, determined to carve her beloved free. If you listen closely at the edge of a deep canyon, you can hear her frantic, whistling cries echoing off the walls. And sometimes, faintly bouncing back from the darkest caverns, you can hear the rhythmic, distant sound of an echo—Kael’s eternal chisel, striking the stone, calling out to let her know he is still waiting.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before canyons possessed voices, the tyrannical God of Silence ruled the towering peaks, demanding absolute quiet. Among the forbidden crags lived Aella, a mischievous wind spirit, who fell deeply in love with a mortal stone-carver named Kael. Kael defied the divine decree not with a flute, but with his chisel. The rhythmic strike of his hammer against the barren rock created joyful, ringing melodies that Aella would gleefully carry across the valleys.

Enraged by this persistent music, the God of Silence struck Kael with a terrible curse, transforming the mortal into a hollow, lifeless cavern at the edge of the deepest gorge. The mountains fell deathly quiet. Heartbroken but fiercely defiant, Aella refused to let her beloved’s music fade into the eternal void.

Knowing she could not break the divine curse, she made the ultimate sacrifice. Aella surrendered her ethereal form, weaving her essence directly into the rushing air of the gorge. She surged through the hollow caverns of Kael’s petrified body, her breath striking the stone walls like his hammer once did. Now, whenever a sound enters the canyon, Aella catches it and sings it back, their eternal defiance forever echoing in the stone.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the deep canyons scarred the earth, the jealous God of Silence sought to banish all sound from the world. Defying this decree, Kael, a master stone-carver, labored tirelessly to build a sanctuary—a magnificent marble labyrinth where melodies could be hidden and preserved forever. Kael’s spirit, trapped within the rock, catches the sounds and sings them back to her. This eternal exchange—the echo—is their defiant love, ensuring the world will never truly be silent.
